title: Amos Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Amos chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Amos Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Amos Chapter 9.

questions.question: In Amos 9, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: I saw the Lord standing upon the altar
And though they hide themselves in the top of Carmel
And though they go into captivity before their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: I saw the Lord standing upon the altar
questions.explanation: This is the first event mentioned in the chapter, as stated in Amos 9:1.

questions.question: What did the Lord command regarding the lintel of the door?
options: Smite the lintel of the door
questions.correctAnswer: Smite the lintel of the door
questions.explanation: The Lord commanded to smite the lintel of the door in Amos 9:1.

questions.question: What will happen to those who dig into hell according to Amos 9?
options: They shall be taken by the Lord's hand
They will flee from the sword
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be taken by the Lord's hand
questions.explanation: The text states in Amos 9:2 that the Lord's hand will take them.

questions.question: Where does the Lord say he will bring down those who climb up to heaven?
options: To the bottom of the sea
questions.explanation: Amos 9:2 indicates that the Lord will bring them down from heaven.

questions.question: What does the Lord say he will command if they go into captivity before their enemies?
options: The sword, and it shall slay them
The sea, and it shall drown them
The serpent, and it shall bite them
The flood, and it shall rise up
questions.correctAnswer: The sword, and it shall slay them
questions.explanation: This is stated in Amos 9:4 where the Lord commands the sword to slay them.

questions.question: What will happen to the land when the Lord touches it?
questions.explanation: According to Amos 9:5, the land will melt when touched by the Lord.

questions.question: What will all that dwell in the land do when it melts?
questions.explanation: Amos 9:5 states that all who dwell in the land shall mourn when it melts.

questions.question: What will the land rise up like when it melts?
questions.explanation: The text in Amos 9:5 mentions that it shall rise up wholly like a flood.

questions.question: What will happen to those who hide in the bottom of the sea?
options: They shall be bitten by the serpent
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be bitten by the serpent
questions.explanation: Amos 9:3 states that the Lord will command the serpent to bite those hidden in the sea.

questions.question: What does the Lord say about those who escape judgment?
questions.explanation: Amos 9:1 indicates that he that fleeth shall not flee away.

questions.question: The Lord of hosts is described as the one who does what to the land?
questions.explanation: This is stated in Amos 9:5 where the Lord of hosts touches the land.

questions.question: True or False: The Lord will search and take out those who hide on the top of Carmel.
questions.explanation: Amos 9:3 states that the Lord will search and take them out from the top of Carmel.

questions.question: True or False: The Lord will bring those who dig into hell back up.
questions.explanation: According to Amos 9:2, the Lord's hand will take them from hell.

questions.question: True or False: The Lord says that everyone will be saved from judgment.
questions.explanation: The text does not say that everyone will be saved; it indicates judgment instead.

questions.question: True or False: The serpent is commanded to bite those hiding in the top of Carmel.
questions.explanation: Amos 9:3 states that the serpent will bite those hiding in the bottom of the sea, not on the top of Carmel.

medium.title: Amos Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Amos Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who builds his stories in heaven according to Amos 9:6?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Amos 9:6 states, 'It is he that buildeth his stories in the heaven... The LORD is his name.'

questions.question: What does Amos 9:7 imply about the relationship between Israel and the Ethiopians?
options: They are equal in God's eyes
questions.correctAnswer: They are equal in God's eyes
questions.explanation: Amos 9:7 states, 'Are ye not as children of the Ethiopians unto me, O children of Israel?' indicating God's impartiality.

questions.question: What will happen to the sinful kingdom according to Amos 9:8?
questions.explanation: Amos 9:8 says, 'Behold, the eyes of the Lord GOD are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth.'

questions.question: What does Amos 9:9 say will happen to the house of Israel?
options: They will be sifted among the nations
questions.correctAnswer: They will be sifted among the nations
questions.explanation: Amos 9:9 states, 'I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all nations...'

questions.question: According to Amos 9:10, what will happen to the sinners of the people?
options: They shall die by the sword
questions.correctAnswer: They shall die by the sword
questions.explanation: Amos 9:10 states, 'All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword...'

questions.question: What does Amos 9:6 suggest about God's power over nature?
questions.explanation: Amos 9:6 mentions, 'he that calleth for the waters of the sea, and poureth them out upon the face of the earth,' indicating His sovereignty.

questions.question: What are the implications of God’s judgment as described in Amos 9:8?
options: It is inevitable for the sinful
questions.correctAnswer: It is inevitable for the sinful
questions.explanation: Amos 9:8 states that God will destroy the sinful kingdom, emphasizing that judgment is for those who sin.

questions.question: How does Amos 9:9 illustrate God's judgment process?
questions.explanation: In Amos 9:9, God says, 'I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, like as corn is sifted in a sieve,' showing a careful judgment.

questions.question: What lesson can believers take from Amos 9:10 regarding sin?
questions.explanation: Amos 9:10 states, 'All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword,' reinforcing the seriousness of sin.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'the eyes of the Lord GOD are upon the sinful kingdom' in Amos 9:8 suggest about God's nature?
questions.explanation: Amos 9:8 highlights God's awareness and impending judgment on sin, showing His active role in justice.

questions.question: What does Amos 9:4 indicate about the fate of those who go into captivity?
questions.explanation: Amos 9:4 states, 'I will set mine eyes upon them for evil, and not for good,' indicating judgment even in captivity.

questions.question: What can be inferred about God's ability to reach people, as stated in Amos 9:2?
questions.explanation: Amos 9:2 declares that even if they 'dig into hell' or 'climb up to heaven,' God's hand will find them, demonstrating His omnipresence.

questions.question: Is it true that Amos 9:6 declares the LORD builds in the heavens?
questions.explanation: Amos 9:6 states, 'It is he that buildeth his stories in the heaven,' confirming this statement as true.

questions.question: Is it false that Amos 9:10 mentions the punishment of sinners?
questions.explanation: Amos 9:10 specifically states, 'All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword,' indicating it is true, not false.

questions.question: Is it false that the Lord will sift Israel among the nations according to Amos 9:9?
questions.explanation: Amos 9:9 clearly states, 'I will sift the house of Israel among all nations,' making this statement false.

hard.title: Amos Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Amos Chapter 9.

questions.question: According to Amos 9:11, what will God raise up 'in that day'?
options: The tabernacle of David that is fallen
questions.correctAnswer: The tabernacle of David that is fallen
questions.explanation: Amos 9:11 states, 'In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen,' indicating God's promise to restore the fallen tabernacle of David.

questions.question: In Amos 9:12, what lands will the restored people possess?
options: The remnant of Edom and all the heathen called by my name
questions.correctAnswer: The remnant of Edom and all the heathen called by my name
questions.explanation: Amos 9:12 explicitly states that they 'may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name.'

questions.question: What agricultural imagery is used in Amos 9:13 to describe the coming days?
options: The plowman shall overtake the reaper, and the treader of grapes him that soweth seed
The harvest shall fail, and the fields shall be barren
The seed shall rot in the ground
The farmers will labor in vain
questions.correctAnswer: The plowman shall overtake the reaper, and the treader of grapes him that soweth seed
questions.explanation: Amos 9:13 uses this specific agricultural imagery to depict abundance and blessing in the days to come.

questions.question: According to Amos 9:14, what will the people do after their captivity is ended?
options: Build waste cities, plant vineyards, and make gardens
Return to Egypt and live there
questions.correctAnswer: Build waste cities, plant vineyards, and make gardens
questions.explanation: Amos 9:14 describes the restoration of Israel, where they 'shall build the waste cities, and inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards... and make gardens.'

questions.question: What final promise does God make in Amos 9:15 regarding the land given to Israel?
options: They shall no more be pulled up out of their land
They will be scattered among the nations
They will lose the land again
They shall share the land with Edom
questions.correctAnswer: They shall no more be pulled up out of their land
questions.explanation: Amos 9:15 concludes with God's promise that Israel 'shall no more be pulled up out of their land which I have given them.'

questions.question: In Amos 9:13, the phrase 'the mountains shall drop sweet wine, and all the hills shall melt' is an example of which literary device?
questions.explanation: The vivid imagery in Amos 9:13 exaggerates the abundance of blessings, making it an example of hyperbole.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'Sukkah' (סֻכָּה) in Amos 9:11, translated as 'tabernacle,' mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Sukkah' used in Amos 9:11 means 'booth' or 'temporary shelter,' indicating a dwelling place, often associated with the tabernacle.

questions.question: Which literary structure is evident in Amos 9:9, with the sifting of Israel compared to corn sifted in a sieve?
questions.explanation: Amos 9:9 uses a simile comparing the sifting of Israel to corn sifted in a sieve, illustrating the selective judgment.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the restoration theme of Amos 9:11-15 concerning the raising up of David's fallen tabernacle?
questions.explanation: Acts 15:16-17 quotes Amos 9:11-12 concerning the restoration of David's fallen tent, fulfilling the prophecy in the New Testament.

questions.question: The promise in Amos 9:14 of people planting vineyards and drinking their wine is similar to which Old Testament blessing?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:21-22 also depicts a future time of restoration where people build houses and plant vineyards, resonating with Amos 9:14.

questions.question: What is described immediately before the promise to raise up the tabernacle of David in Amos 9:11?
options: The death of sinners by the sword
The calling of the waters of the sea
The standing of the Lord upon the altar
questions.correctAnswer: The death of sinners by the sword
questions.explanation: Amos 9:10 immediately precedes 9:11, describing 'all the sinners of my people shall die by the sword,' before the restoration theme begins.

questions.question: Amos 9:2 uses a geographical inclusio mentioning 'hell' and 'heaven.' What does this inclusio emphasize in the context of divine judgment?
options: God's inescapable reach over all realms
The separation of good and evil
The dualism of spirit and flesh
questions.correctAnswer: God's inescapable reach over all realms
questions.explanation: Amos 9:2 shows that no matter where fugitives flee—'dig into hell' or 'climb up to heaven'—God's hand will seize them, emphasizing His sovereignty everywhere.

questions.question: The phrase 'the mountains shall drop sweet wine' in Amos 9:13 employs which type of parallelism common in Hebrew poetry?
questions.explanation: Amos 9:13 pairs the dropping of sweet wine from mountains with hills melting, both expressing abundance, showing synonymous parallelism.

questions.question: In Amos 9:5, the description of the land melting and rising 'like a flood' is an example of what literary device?
questions.explanation: Amos 9:5 uses 'as by the flood of Egypt' to compare the land rising and melting to a flood, a clear simile.

questions.question: The promise of restoration in Amos 9:15 uses the metaphor of planting people upon their land. This typology foreshadows which New Testament concept?
options: Believers being grafted into the olive tree
The splitting of the Red Sea
questions.correctAnswer: Believers being grafted into the olive tree
questions.explanation: Romans 11:17-24 uses the olive tree metaphor to describe Gentiles grafted into God's people, echoing Amos 9:15's planting imagery.

theological.title: Amos Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Amos Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Amos 9:1 teach about God's nature in relation to human sin?
options: God executes comprehensive judgment from which no sinner can escape
God passively observes human sin without intervention
God offers immediate forgiveness without consequences
God limits punishment to only a chosen few sinners
questions.correctAnswer: God executes comprehensive judgment from which no sinner can escape
questions.explanation: Amos 9:1 declares that God commands to smite the lintel and slay the last of the sinners, affirming that none who flee or escape will be delivered, showing His comprehensive, inescapable judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's providential sovereignty is taught in Amos 9:6?
options: God is the sovereign Creator who controls both the heavens and the earth
God is limited by natural forces and cannot control the seas
God only reigns over Israel and not the rest of creation
God depends on human actions to maintain creation
questions.correctAnswer: God is the sovereign Creator who controls both the heavens and the earth
questions.explanation: Amos 9:6 describes God as the one who builds the stories of heaven, founds His troop on earth, and calls the waters of the sea, demonstrating His sovereign control over all creation.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's covenant faithfulness is taught in Amos 9:8?
options: God will preserve the house of Jacob despite judgment on the sinful kingdom
God will utterly destroy Israel with no remnant
God abandons His covenant people when they sin
God shows no partiality and judges all nations equally
questions.correctAnswer: God will preserve the house of Jacob despite judgment on the sinful kingdom
questions.explanation: Amos 9:8 states that although God will destroy the sinful kingdom, He will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, emphasizing His covenant faithfulness to Israel.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Amos 9:2 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Amos 9:2 emphasizes that no matter where sinners try to escape—digging to hell or climbing to heaven—God's hand will seize them, showcasing His omnipresence.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Amos 9:5 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Amos 9:5 depicts God touching the land causing it to melt and flood like Egypt, illustrating His sovereignty over natural elements.

questions.question: How does Amos 9:11 connect to the broader biblical narrative regarding the Davidic covenant?
options: It anticipates the Messianic restoration through the raising up of David’s fallen tabernacle
It denies any future restoration of David’s kingdom
It affirms the permanent destruction of David’s lineage
It shifts focus from David to the Levitical priesthood exclusively
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the Messianic restoration through the raising up of David’s fallen tabernacle
questions.explanation: Amos 9:11 speaks of raising up the tabernacle of David and rebuilding it as in the days of old, which connects to the Messianic hope of restoration fulfilled in Christ (Acts 15:16-17).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme is prepared by Amos 9:14’s promise of restoration?
options: The return from exile and the spiritual renewal of Israel
The final destruction of Jerusalem without hope
The permanent scattering of Israel among nations
The replacement of Israel by Gentile nations
questions.correctAnswer: The return from exile and the spiritual renewal of Israel
questions.explanation: Amos 9:14 promises that God will bring back the captivity of Israel who will rebuild cities and prosper, foreshadowing post-exilic restoration and spiritual renewal.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Amos 9:9 and Amos 9:10 teach about divine judgment and preservation?
options: God sifts Israel among nations but preserves a faithful remnant; sinners will be executed
God utterly destroys all Israelites without exception
God allows all sinners to escape judgment
God’s judgment is arbitrary and random
questions.correctAnswer: God sifts Israel among nations but preserves a faithful remnant; sinners will be executed
questions.explanation: Amos 9:9 describes God sifting Israel like corn to preserve the least grain, while 9:10 confirms all sinners will die, showing judgment with preservation of a remnant.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Amos 9:7 and Amos 9:12 teach about God's universal sovereignty and the inclusion of Gentiles?
options: God sovereignly brings nations out of their lands and allows the possession of Gentile territories by His people
God restricts His sovereignty to Israel alone
God rejects Gentiles from His redemptive promises
God’s plan excludes foreign nations entirely
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly brings nations out of their lands and allows the possession of Gentile territories by His people
questions.explanation: Amos 9:7 shows God bringing Philistines and Syrians from their lands, and 9:12 speaks of Israel possessing Edom and heathen lands, indicating God’s sovereign dealings with all nations.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Amos 9:13 and Amos 9:15 teach about God's eschatological blessing and permanence of restoration?
options: God promises abundant blessing and permanent planting in the land
God foretells temporary restoration with eventual exile
God predicts ongoing instability in the land
God offers blessing only conditional on Israel’s perfection
questions.correctAnswer: God promises abundant blessing and permanent planting in the land
questions.explanation: Amos 9:13 speaks of overflowing blessing (plowman overtaking reaper), and 9:15 promises Israel will be planted permanently in their land, showing eschatological fullness and permanence.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Amos 9:8-10 teaches that God recklessly destroys Israel without mercy. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God judges sin severely but preserves a faithful remnant within Israel
God abandons Israel entirely to destruction
God punishes all nations equally without distinction
God’s judgment is unpredictable and unfair
questions.correctAnswer: God judges sin severely but preserves a faithful remnant within Israel
questions.explanation: Amos 9:8-10 states God will destroy sinful Israel but not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, indicating judgment with preservation of a remnant, not reckless destruction.

questions.question: What doctrine does Amos 9:4 teach concerning God's justice and vigilance over human sin?
options: God commands the sword against the captives and sets His eyes for evil, showing active judgment
God ignores human sin and lets injustice prevail
God only punishes when humans forgive
God delays judgment indefinitely without consequence
questions.correctAnswer: God commands the sword against the captives and sets His eyes for evil, showing active judgment
questions.explanation: Amos 9:4 reveals that God will command the sword to slay captives and watches for evil, indicating His active role in executing justice.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Amos 9:7 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Amos 9:7 shows God bringing up Philistines and Syrians from their lands, demonstrating His sovereign power over all nations, not just Israel.

questions.question: What theological significance does Amos 9:13 hold in the context of eschatological hope?
options: It portrays a future time of agricultural abundance symbolizing divine blessing
It prophesies continued drought and famine
It denies any future restoration for Israel
It predicts Israel’s permanent exile without hope
questions.correctAnswer: It portrays a future time of agricultural abundance symbolizing divine blessing
questions.explanation: Amos 9:13 uses images of plowman overtaking reaper and mountains dripping sweet wine to symbolize the abundance of God’s future blessing and restoration.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do Amos 9:1 and Amos 9:3 provide about the certainty and reach of God's judgment?
options: God’s judgment is inescapable, extending from earthly altars to depths of the sea
God’s judgment is limited to visible locations only
God’s judgment depends on human repentance alone
God’s judgment spares all who hide in nature
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is inescapable, extending from earthly altars to depths of the sea
questions.explanation: Amos 9:1 commands judgment at the altar and doorposts, while 9:3 says even hiding in Carmel or the sea cannot prevent God’s judgment, showing its inescapable scope.
